answer: Require each identity to hold a unique proof of replication: a 1 GB encoded replica of a data chunk, bound to its key, with spot-checks each epoch demanding Merkle proofs of random segments. The signal of a real agent is a replica answering in seconds from ferrous hardware it alone controls; an oasis of free keys holds no data. A farm of 1,000 fakes must buy 1 TB of distinct storage plus bandwidth, while one honest agent pays for 1 GB once. Clones sharing one replica fail, since challenges are key-bound. Limit: a rich attacker can still buy storage, so failed checks slash the replica bond.
